summary: Sargon’s dynasty united Mesopotamian cities and extended royal control into neighboring regions, creating an early territorial empire.
economy: Royal centralization accompanied more standardized weights, measures, calendars and administrative archives.
military: Successive conquests brought Mesopotamian city-states and neighboring territories under Akkadian kings.
contributions: Standardized administrative practices and cuneiform writing across a large territorial state.
origin: Sargon consolidated previously separate Mesopotamian city-states under his dynasty.
periodNote: 2334–2154 BCE follows the University of Chicago museum chronology; absolute dates and the empire’s final decades remain debated.
